findings.finding: The FY27 bar is modest and management has already sized it. Company-compiled consensus has FY27 op profit at £502m (+3.5% on FY26's £485m) with margin down 150bp to 25.0% on revenue +9.8%. On 16 July the CEO said FY27 reverts 'towards our financial model ... broadly where market consensus is right now', and the CFO said margins 'will moderate a bit'. That makes an in-line first guide the base case, with the wide range (470-545) the source of the tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prelims, which carry the first guide: Nov 2023 +11.19%, Nov 2024 -7.98%, Nov 2025 +0.57% (the last after a conservative initial FY26 guide of 6% organic and c.22.5% margin, later raised three times). Large in both directions.
findings.original_quote: FY27 ... Adjusted operating profit (£m) 502 470 545 ... Adjusted operating margin (%) 25.0% 24.1% 26.0% ... Last updated: 20 October 2026 * Based on forecasts by 16 covering analysts.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The consensus and the July comment are both public, so the in-line base case is in the price. What is not priced is which end of a £75m-wide range the company picks. If the market had priced a cut, the stock would trade below where it did after the July comment. Instead it sits about where it was in late October, after a sector-wide fall (Halma, Weir, Rolls-Royce).
findings.independence: Same signal from a different document: the Q3 call transcript, 'you should expect that we'll revert back towards our financial model for next year, which is broadly where market consensus is right now' (https://www.diplomaplc.com/media/ym1ao0mc/diploma-q3-transcript-160726.pdf, 2026-07-16). One fact, so it is filed once.

findings.finding: FY26 is pre-released and consensus sits on the guide. Q3 RNS: organic 14%, margin c.26.5%, operating profit growth c.42%. Consensus FY26 op profit is £485m in a tight 481-493 range. The reported year carries no new information unless the outturn leaves the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26 has been raised three times (Mar +13%, May +6%, Jul +7% to consensus). Each raise moved the stock (+3.2% H1, +6.3% Q3). A print at the guide has not been tested this year.
findings.original_quote: Further upgrade to FY26 guidance (at constant currency): Organic revenue growth of 14% - up from 12% ... Operating margin of c.26.5% - up from c.25% Operating profit growth of c.42%
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. That is why it is sized at 0. The only unpriced part would be a print outside 481-493, and nothing found says one is coming. The CFO said Peerless 'started H2 better than expected', but that was already folded into the July raise.
findings.independence: Consensus page FY26 £485m / 26.5% matches the guide: https://www.diplomaplc.com/investors/analyst-consensus/

findings.finding: Into the print the stock fell 12% from its 16 Oct peak (7890p to 6890p by 23 Oct; spot 7180p, -7.95% over 20d) on sector days with no company news. Disclosed shorts are covering (1.88% to 1.58%). Capital Group sold down to 12.95% inside the drawdown while FMR had built to 7.65% in September. The derating has lowered the bar for an in-line guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior case on this name of a pre-print drawdown of this size. The Nov 2024 prelims (-7.98%) came without one.
findings.original_quote: The Capital Group Companies, Inc. ... Resulting situation on the date on which threshold was crossed or reached 12.948337 ... Position of previous notification 13.817392
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is the price. The claim is only that sector selling, not a company fact, set it, which asymmetrically lowers the bar for an in-line guide. If the market expected a below-consensus guide, shorts would be building into the print, and they are covering. Capital Group's selling is the counterweight and is why this is small.

findings.finding: Aerospace read-across to Peerless: on 23 Oct Safran's Q3 raised investor concern that aftermarket growth slows into 2027 as airlines cut capacity on high fuel prices. Rolls-Royce fell 6.5% and Diploma 2.7% that morning. Diploma already guides Peerless to moderate to 'high single digit 10-ish percent'. A weaker FY27 Peerless line could pressure the margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Diploma sold off in sympathy with Rolls-Royce on the Safran day (-2.7% midday 23 Oct). Peerless moderation was flagged in March and July and the stock still rose on those updates.
findings.original_quote: Rolls-Royce was sharply lower after French peer Safran warned of softening growth in the wide-body jet market.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Diploma traded down on the day. This is a proxy, and Peerless is one business inside Controls. The rest of the group grew 10% organically excluding Peerless (Q3 call), so the net effect on the group guide is a fraction of the Safran headline.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' (reported_quarter 4 of 14): FY26 finding cut from +0.2 to 0.0, since the period is pre-released and consensus sits on the guide.

'The move is in the guide' and the first-guide-for-a-new-year rule (median 9.0% on guidance events): abs_move_pct raised from 6.0 to 7.0. It is held below 9 because the CEO pre-signalled FY27 as in line with consensus.
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' and the net-of-the-company rule: Safran/aerospace proxy trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3, since Peerless is one business and ex-Peerless organic was 10%.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): checked H1 FCF conversion (76%) and added cash_flow as an unknown line in new_in_release. No signed finding, because no full-year evidence exists.
